newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian markets bullish after Yeltsin surgery.
newsitem.headline: Russian markets bullish after Yeltsin surgery.

text.p: Russian financial markets rose on Tuesday on news that President Boris Yeltsin had survived bypass heart surgery and doctors predicted he would make a full recovery.
Shares mostly recovered from a mid-afternoon sell-off by Western investors that some dealers said was triggered in large part by sell limits.
Long Treasury bills, where prices rose in morning trade, could continue the trend on Wednesday, dealers said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose almost two percent on a fairly robust $23 million trade volume.
"There is still a large appetite for Russian risk," said Jim Nail, head of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
But equity traders said new investors were unlikely to swoop into the market over the next few days during Yeltsin's expected recovery.

"The success of the operation is only half of the deal. Very few doubted it would go wrong, but how the rehabilitation period will go, that's the question," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at Prospekt.
Yeltsin had more than four bypasses during the operation, according to surgeon Renat Akchurin, and many doctors said full recovery was probable but not guaranteed.
The president's health has dominated share market trends since Yeltsin announced in September he would have surgery.

Analysts said the shares market, which suffered a huge fall after July's presidential election when Western investors took profits on over-valued stocks, was not likely to fall because it was not similarly over-priced.
"The market is in a very good, balanced condition," said Alexander Babayan, strategy investor at CentreInvest Securities.
Dealers said the market for Treasury bills, or GKOs, where long paper yields eased in morning trade, could show more price growth.

"The market closed before announcements of the operation's success came out, so there is still room for long yields to go down by one to two percent in the next two trading sessions, on Wednesday and Sunday," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell trader Sergei Ivanov.
Russian markets are closed on Thursday and Friday but will be open on Sunday and will have an abbreviated trading session on Wednesday.
Yields on the longest T-bill, which matures in June 1997, closed at 56.26 after 57.99 at the previous session's close.
Short-term paper yields went up as investors moved into the longer paper, a trend which dealers said would probably continue.
The GKO market, which unlike shares is dominated by domestic investors, is preparing for greater foreign participation which is likely to make the market more sensitive to news of Yeltsin.
Dealers in Minfin bonds said prices had firmed up to two big figures in early trading and a further 0.35-0.50 point after surgery ended.
"The rise is noteworthy as trading is still thin," said one dealer. The market is still cautious since authorities have frozen $74 million worth of bonds in the $11 billion market.
Pressure on the rouble eased and the currency firmed against the dollar after news of the operation's initial success appeared.
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,463-64 per dollar after 5,464-66 late on Monday.
